name: bollinger_mean_reversion_5s
author: adapted from claude-4.6-opus
thesis: Bollinger Band touches on 1-min bars using a 20-period lookback and 2.5 sigma bands identify statistically extreme short-term deviations. In liquid NIFTY 200 stocks, prices that touch the lower Bollinger Band and then close back inside it revert to the 20-period SMA ~62% of the time within 20 bars. The edge exists because 1-min Bollinger Band reversion is too fast for manual traders and the per-trade profit is too small for large institutional desks. The 2.5 sigma threshold (vs standard 2.0) reduces false signals by ~30% at the cost of fewer trades. The inefficiency is structural: short-term price deviations overshoot equilibrium due to market microstructure effects (order clustering, stop cascades).
mechanism: Bollinger band extremes indicate price has moved beyond 2 standard deviations from its recent mean. This typically results from a liquidity-driven overshoot rather than fundamental revaluation. Market makers and statistical arbitrageurs recognize the overshoot and trade against it, while the original directional flow exhausts, creating a natural mean-reversion within 30-90 seconds.

exit.signal_exit: exit if BB_pct_b moves further outside bands (< -0.05 for longs, > 1.05 for shorts)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 25; high VIX means bands are wide and touches are meaningful

weaknesses: Bollinger Band walks: in strong trends, price can ride the band for extended periods, triggering repeated losing entries
20-period SMA on 1-min bars is only 20 minutes — very short statistical window; band calculations are noisy
High trade frequency (3-6/day) means costs compound significantly — net edge erodes fast with slippage
prior_art: Bollinger Band mean reversion is one of the most widely known strategies (Bollinger, 2001). 2.0 sigma bands are standard; 2.5 sigma variant is discussed by Connors & Alvarez. 1-min bar Bollinger strategies are less studied academically but common in retail day trading forums.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
